correctness.rationale: Norming-face duality computes the derivative. A Julia orthogonal dilation combined with minimal unit-vector rotation proves a quantitative contraction-completion lemma in arbitrary real Hilbert dimensions. A one-parameter quadratic optimization gives the universal upper bound; explicit normalized rank-one perturbations attain both regimes, with the scalar boundary addressed separately. The standalone rational checks and randomized matrix tests were executed but are corroboration, not infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The primary 2022 USSD theorem guarantees an unspecified uniform small-increment bound. This complete all-scale sharp modulus yields a dimension-independent quantitative remainder, an exact phase boundary at t=2, rank-one equality cases and a scalar/non-scalar separation. It provides a reusable contraction-completion lemma and strengthens the qualitative geometric result for two-factor Hilbert tensors.
